leads.f: Who are the Quran's Sabians?
leads.n: The Quran names the Sabians (al-Ṣābiʾūn) beside Jews and Christians. Candidates include the Mandaeans, the pagans of Harran, and Elchasaite baptists.
leads.s: الصابئون · ṣba · to baptize, immerse · Quran 2:62; 5:69; 22:17

leads.f: Whoever saves one life
leads.n: Mishnah Sanhedrin 4:5 teaches that destroying one life is like destroying a world, and saving one is like saving a world. Quran 5:32 states the same principle as decreed for the Children of Israel.
leads.s: judaism -> islam · sanctity-of-life

leads.f: Dara Shikoh's Upanishads reach Schopenhauer
leads.n: Dara Shikoh translated 50 Upanishads into Persian as the Sirr-i Akbar (1657). Anquetil-Duperron's Latin version (Oupnek'hat, 1801–02) is how Schopenhauer read them.
leads.s: hinduism -> islam -> western-philosophy · unity-of-being · self-and-absolute · Dara Shikoh, Sirr-i Akbar (1657); Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn (1655) · Anquetil-Duperron, Oupnek'hat; Schopenhauer

leads.f: Seven Sleepers and the People of the Cave
leads.n: Youths fleeing persecution sleep in a cave for centuries and wake to a changed world. Told in Syriac (Jacob of Serugh), Greek, and Latin sources, and in Quran 18:9–26.
leads.s: sleepers-in-cave · miraculous-sleep · dog-companion · Jacob of Serugh, homily on the Sleepers of Ephesus · Gregory of Tours, Passio septem dormientium

leads.f: tannūr: the oven that boiled at the Flood
leads.n: Akkadian tinūru (oven) reached Aramaic, Hebrew, and Arabic. In the Quran's Noah narrative the sign of the Flood is that the tannūr boiled over.
leads.s: ane-akkadian -> aramaic/hebrew -> islam · boiling-flood-waters · תַּנּוּר · tannûr · تنّور · Quran 11:40 · Quran 23:27

leads.f: Plotinus as the 'Theology of Aristotle'
leads.n: An Arabic paraphrase of Plotinus' Enneads IV–VI circulated as the 'Theology of Aristotle' (al-Kindi's circle, 9th c.) and shaped Islamic Neoplatonism.
leads.s: greco-roman -> islam · the-one · emanation · intellect · Plotinus, Enneads IV–VI · Uthūlūjiyā Arisṭāṭālīs

leads.f: Ancient treaty form and Deuteronomy's covenant
leads.n: Deuteronomy follows the structure of ancient Near Eastern vassal treaties: preamble, history, stipulations, deposit, witnesses, curses and blessings.
leads.s: treaty-form · Hittite vassal treaties (14th–13th c. BCE) · Esarhaddon's Succession Treaty (672 BCE)
